newsitem.title: CANADA: Canadian House to vote on MMT ban on Monday.
newsitem.headline: Canadian House to vote on MMT ban on Monday.

text.p: The Canadian House of Commons will hold a final vote on Monday on a bill which would effectively ban the gasoline additive MMT, the federal government said on Friday.

Debate on the bill, which would ban the import of and interprovincial trade in MMT -- methylcyclopentadienyl manganese tricarbonyl, an octane enhancer -- was curtailed on Friday by the Liberal government in an effort to speed the bill's passage over the objections of the opposition.
The government commands a majority in the elected House of Commons, so passage of the bill is almost certain.
The bill would then proceed to Parliament's upper chamber, the unelected Senate, which usually passes House bills, but occasionally delays or rejects them.
The ban is supported by a coalition of health groups, environmentalists and car manufacturers.
Environmentalists back the claims of automakers that MMT gums up auto emission diagnostic systems, and charge that manganese is a potential neurotoxin that might hamper human brain development.
MMT is made by Ethyl Corp, and imported into Canada by its subsidiary, Ethyl Canada.
